entries.test: Public evaluations of Sora's physical consistency and generalization would establish its current failures or demonstrate a later version reliably handling physics.
entries.note: He reaffirms his earlier prediction. A convincing later demonstration could falsify the indefinite negative forecast.

entries.test: The February 2024 Sora videos would show whether multiple depicted events violate or are implausible under real-world physics.
entries.note: This is an endorsed quotation of his own writing. The factual core concerns visible errors, despite the evaluative phrase 'deeply amiss'.

entries.test: Public evaluations of later Sora versions would show whether they reliably preserve objects across occlusion and camera movement despite extensive training.
entries.note: The surrounding examples give object permanence a concrete behavioral meaning.

entries.test: Public Sora videos and systematic evaluations would establish whether unexplained object disappearances and continuity failures recur across distinct scenes.
entries.note: The plain reading is recurring failures, not failure in every video.

entries.test: Brownlee's review footage, the Mashable report, and December 2024 Sora outputs would show whether the earlier physics and object-permanence failures persisted.
entries.note: He endorses an observation based on reporting. 'Appears' preserves his evidential qualification.

entries.test: Publicly documented Sora training comparisons would show whether increasing training data alone produces reliable physical consistency.
entries.note: Success involving other substantial changes would not by itself refute the claim about more data.

entries.test: Public technical documentation, implementations, and formal guarantees would establish whether generative AI systems can encode and guarantee the stated constraints.
entries.note: Improved compliance alone would not establish a guarantee.

entries.test: Comparative evaluations and public outputs from February and December 2024 would show whether Sora's physics failures remained reproducible after further development.
entries.note: The February-to-December interval is supplied by the surrounding discussion.

entries.test: Public training descriptions and physics evaluations of Sora and earlier sensory-data-based models would show whether repeated attempts failed to acquire reliable physical competence.
entries.note: The plain contextual reading concerns repeated empirical failures, not a proof that learning physics from sensory data is impossible.
He explicitly qualifies the billion-dollar figure with 'perhaps' and 'if I had to guess'.
